blocks.text: Museum de Fundatie in the Netherlands invites applications for a Curator of Contemporary Art to develop exhibitions, expand art-historical perspectives and engage diverse audiences across its locations in Zwolle and Heino.
Open Call:

Museum de Fundatie is recruiting a Curator of Contemporary Art with broad art-historical knowledge, an international outlook and an interest in exploring new approaches to contemporary artistic practice.

The appointed curator will contribute to the museum’s exhibition programme, collection research and publications, developing projects that connect artists, ideas and audiences. The position calls for an experienced professional who can combine independent research with collaborative exhibition-making, translating critical perspectives into accessible and engaging presentations. Particular emphasis is placed on knowledge of artistic practices beyond Europe and the United States, along with an understanding of contemporary developments in the international art world.
Institutional Context:
Museum de Fundatie is an art museum in the Netherlands, operating across two locations: Museum de Fundatie in Zwolle and Kasteel het Nijenhuis in Heino.

Its collection comprises more than 16,000 objects, spanning the late Middle Ages to the present and representing artistic traditions from different parts of the world. Through exhibitions, public programmes, education and research, the museum seeks to make art accessible to broad audiences while encouraging critical engagement with contemporary society.

The institution is examining its future direction through questions of representation, accessibility and the relationship between local histories and international artistic perspectives. The collection remains central to this process, providing a foundation for new research, exhibitions and approaches to interpretation.
Eligibility and Criteria :
Applicants must demonstrate substantial knowledge of contemporary art, strong research capabilities and experience in curatorial practice.
Essential requirements include:
A completed academic degree in art history, at least at master’s level.
A minimum of three years of relevant professional experience as a curator or in a comparable role within the museum or arts sector.
Demonstrable experience in art-historical research and developing exhibitions and publications.
Knowledge of contemporary artistic practices beyond Europe and the United States.
The ability to translate research and ideas into engaging exhibitions, texts and audience-focused presentations.
Strong organisational and communication skills, including experience managing projects, budgets and deadlines.
Ability to initiate projects independently while collaborating with colleagues, artists, researchers, and external partners.
An established national or international professional network, or the capacity and ambition to develop one.
Excellent written and spoken English, basic Dutch communication skills and a willingness to improve Dutch proficiency.
The museum seeks a curator who approaches art history critically, demonstrates intellectual curiosity and is willing to experiment with new perspectives.
Museum de Fundatie encourages applications regardless of background, age, gender, religion, neurodiversity or disability.
Evaluation Process:
Museum de Fundatie will review applications, and shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews scheduled for 11 and 17 December 2026.
The published vacancy does not specify the selection committee’s composition or a detailed assessment framework.
Candidates should show how their experience, research interests, and curatorial approach align with the museum’s commitment to artistic enquiry, collaboration, and accessibility.
Practical Information:
Position: Curator of Contemporary Art
Institution: Museum de Fundatie
Location: Zwolle and Heino, the Netherlands
Working hours: 36 hours per week
Application deadline: 29 November 2026
Interview dates: 11 and 17 December 2026
Contract: Initial one-year appointment, with the possibility of extension and permanent employment.
Salary: Scale 11 of the Dutch Museum Collective Labour Agreement (Museum-cao), depending on qualifications and experience.

The position offers an opportunity to work with the museum’s collection of more than 16,000 objects, collaborate with an established team and contribute to exhibitions and research across its two locations.
Applications and Queries:
Application deadline: 29 November 2026 .
Candidates are required to submit:
A curriculum vitae (CV).
A motivation letter.
Submit both documents in PDF format.
Send applications to: vacature@museumdefundatie.nl
For the attention of: Beatrice von Bormann, Managing Director.
Official vacancy information: https://museumdefundatie.nl/en/about-museum/work-us
Please direct questions about the position to the same email address.
